contents.name: What is Sound?
contents.text_content:
{"time":1795420004930,"blocks":[{"type":"header","data":{"text":"Sounds of Animals & Birds","level":2}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"“Sound is the vocabulary of Nature.”
— Pierre Schaeffer"}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Let us find out what sound really is."}},{"type":"header","data":{"text":"What is sound?","level":3}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Sound is a form of energy that we can hear. It is made when something vibrates or moves quickly. We hear many different sounds around us every day. For example, people talking, birds chirping, rain falling, music playing, and animals making sounds. Sound is very important because it helps us communicate, learn new things, and understand the world around us."}},{"type":"header","data":{"text":"Now, let us learn about animal and bird sounds. 🐶🐦","level":3}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Animals and birds use sounds to communicate with one another in their daily life. Different animals make different sounds to express their feelings, warn others of danger, find food, protect themselves, and call their friends or family members. Just like we use words to talk, animals and birds also use sounds to share messages."}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"By listening carefully to these sounds, we can learn more about their feelings and actions. So, let us enjoy listening and discovering the amazing sounds of animals and birds! 🎶✨"}}],"version":"2.29.1"}

{"time":1795432912904,"blocks":[{"type":"header","data":{"text":"PARTS OF SPEECH","level":2}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Words are like building blocks of sentences. Every word we use has a special job to do. These jobs are called Parts of Speech. Learning parts of speech helps us speak and write English correctly and creatively."}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"In this module, students will learn about the eight parts of speech through fun explanations, games, activities, examples, and practice exercises."}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Let’s explore the world of words!"}},{"type":"image","data":{"file":{"url":"{{APP_URL}}/storage/contents/images/6b03f688d4227-1795421832.svg"},"caption":"The eight parts of speech","withBorder":false,"stretched":false,"withBackground":false}},{"type":"table","data":{"withHeadings":true,"content":[["Part of Speech","Definition","Examples","Example in Sentence"],["Noun
(also known as ‘naming word’)","A noun is a naming word used to identify a person, place, animal, thing, or idea. Nouns help us talk about people, objects, feelings, and places around us. They are one of the most important parts of a sentence because they often act as the subject or object.","teacher, Chennai, book, tiger, honesty","1. The teacher explained the lesson clearly.
2. Chennai is known for its rich cultural heritage.
3. I borrowed a book from the library.
4. The tiger is the national animal of India.
5. Honesty is the best policy."],["Pronoun","A pronoun is a word used in place of a noun to avoid repeating the same noun again and again in a sentence. Pronouns make sentences shorter, smoother, and easier to understand.","he, she, they, it, we, you, them, your, our, us, him, his, her, their, mine, myself, yourself, themselves","1. He won the first prize in the competition.

{"time":1795430094222,"blocks":[{"type":"header","data":{"text":"COMPOUND WORDS 🌻","level":2}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Did you know that some words are made by combining two smaller words? The combined word often has a meaning that goes beyond the sum of its parts.","For example, a blackbird is a specific type of bird, not just any bird that’s black. A greenhouse isn’t simply a house that’s green. It’s a structure with a specific function.","There are three types of compound words, they are:"]}},{"type":"list","data":{"style":"ordered","items":["Closed compound word","Hyphenated compound word","Open compound word"]}},{"type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Closed compounds combine two words into a single unit with no space or hyphen. These are the most common types in everyday English.
Examples include: notebook, sunflower, toothbrush etc.","Hyphenated compounds are formed by joining two or more words with a hyphen (-). The hyphen shows that the words work together as a single unit to express one idea.
Examples include: mother-in-law, editor-in-chief, ex-husband, on-line, Ex-MLA etc.","Open compounds are two words that function as a single concept but are written with a space between them.
Examples include: ice cream, post office, high school, full moon, bus stop etc."]}}],"version":"2.29.1"}

contents.name: Welcome to Intermediate Listening
contents.text_content: {"time":1795431843518,"blocks":[{"type":"header","data":{"text":"Listening Skill 🎧","level":2}},{"type":"image","data":{"file":{"url":"{{APP_URL}}/storage/contents/images/6b041d983d4e3-1795431832.svg"},"caption":"Let’s listen!","withBorder":false,"stretched":false,"withBackground":false}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"In Level 1, we developed our basic listening abilities by identifying sounds, words, and simple instructions. Now, it is time to take our listening skills to the next level."}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Listening is more than simply hearing words. It involves paying attention, understanding meaning, recognizing emotions, and interpreting the speaker’s purpose. Effective listening helps us communicate confidently, follow conversations, learn new information, and respond appropriately in different situations."}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"In this module, you will listen to conversations, stories, and different types of sentences. You will learn to identify important details, arrange events in the correct sequence, and recognize how sentences are used to express information, ask questions, give instructions, or show emotions. The activities move from guided listening to independent comprehension."}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Let’s get started!"}}],"version":"2.29.1"}

contents.name: Types of Sentences
contents.text_content: {"time":1795431843746,"blocks":[{"type":"header","data":{"text":"TYPES OF SENTENCES","level":2}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Every conversation is made up of different kinds of sentences. Let’s discover how they work!"}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"In everyday communication, we express our thoughts through sentences. A sentence is a group of words arranged according to grammatical rules to convey a complete and meaningful idea. Learning the correct word order often requires practice, as English follows a fairly fixed sentence structure. Changing the order of words can alter the intended meaning or make the sentence sound unnatural and awkward."}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Sentences serve different purposes in communication. We use them to express opinions, ask questions, give commands, or show strong feelings and emotions. Based on their function, sentences in English are classified into four main types. Let us explore these types and learn how they are used in everyday communication."}},{"type":"list","data":{"style":"ordered","items":["Declarative / Assertive","Interrogative","Imperative","Exclamatory"]}}],"version":"2.29.1"}

contents.name: Declarative Sentences
contents.text_content: {"time":1795431843959,"blocks":[{"type":"header","data":{"text":"DECLARATIVE SENTENCES","level":2}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"A declarative sentence is used to express an opinion, share information, or make a statement. In writing, it begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop (.). Declarative sentences can be written in any tense and may be either affirmative (positive) or negative."}},{"type":"header","data":{"text":"Affirmative Declarative Sentences","level":3}},{"type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["My mom cooks delicious food.","She is my best friend.","We are going to the museum tomorrow.","They completed the project on time."]}},{"type":"header","data":{"text":"Negative Declarative Sentences","level":3}},{"type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["I can’t ride a bike.","She is not at home today.","We do not watch television during study hours.","They have not finished their homework yet."]}}],"version":"2.29.1"}

contents.name: Interrogative, Imperative & Exclamatory Sentences
contents.text_content: {"time":1795432913521,"blocks":[{"type":"header","data":{"text":"INTERROGATIVE SENTENCES","level":2}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"An interrogative sentence is a type of sentence that asks a question. It usually begins with a question word (who, what, where, when, why, how) and ends with a question mark (?). You can also use auxiliary verbs to start a question (yes/no questions), and you can use all tenses in these sentences too."}},{"type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Where is my car?","Have you ever been to New York?","Who painted this beautiful picture?"]}},{"type":"header","data":{"text":"IMPERATIVE SENTENCES","level":2}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"Imperative sentences are used to issue a command or instruction, make a request, or offer advice. These sentences also provide direction. They usually end with a full stop (.) or an exclamation mark (!). Imperative sentences typically begin with verbs, as the subject (the person the sentence refers to) is implied."}},{"type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["Get your hands up! (Command)","Do your homework. (Instruction)","Close the window. (Request or demand)","Please come with me for dinner. (Invitation)"]}},{"type":"header","data":{"text":"EXCLAMATORY SENTENCES","level":2}},{"type":"paragraph","data":{"text":"An exclamatory sentence expresses a strong emotion. It can be a surprise, a shock, or even anger. When listening, you can identify an exclamatory sentence right away — the tone of the person’s voice will indicate it. But in writing, you need to use the exclamation mark (!). Here are a few examples of exclamatory sentences:"}},{"type":"list","data":{"style":"unordered","items":["What a delicious cookie!","She is so beautiful!","What a cute
